input.quote: Neither Party may terminate this Agreement during the Initial Term except as set forth in paragraph 4(b) or any Exhibit. Either Party may terminate this Agreement for any reason following the Initial Term upon ninety (90) days written notice to the other Party. Except for termination for material breach as detailed in paragraph 4(b), Kubient shall be entitled to all fees generated during the termination period regardless of which Party terminates the Agreement,
input.rationale: Paragraph 4(a) is the only convenience-termination mechanic in the Agreement, and it fails the fallback in two respects: AP has no no-cause exit at all during the Initial Term (the lock-in is mutual and the 90-day right only operates "following the Initial Term"), and Kubient's post-Initial Term right is untethered to term-end, so it can walk away mid-renewal-term (an auto-renewal/notice right is not term-end-only unless the effective date is expressly anchored to the end of the then-current term). Our single edit confines the Initial Term lock-in to Kubient, deletes "following the Initial Term" so AP may terminate for convenience at any time on 90 days' notice, and adds a proviso confining any Kubient termination under that sentence to the end of the then-current Term. The mutual 90 days' written notice to the other Party is retained verbatim, so Kubient must still give AP 90 days' notice, and the retained fee sentence entitles Kubient only to fees generated during the termination period (revenue earned through the 90-day notice window), so no early-termination fee exceeding three months' fees exists. We do not pursue the preferred level (30 days' notice and pro-rata refund of prepaid fees), which is a poor fit for this revenue-share structure with no prepaid fees; the redline therefore lands at the fallback.

proposal.summary: Give AP a 90-day no-cause exit at any time and confine Kubient's convenience termination to the end of the then-current Term.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have limited the Initial Term lock-in to Kubient and removed the "following the Initial Term" restriction so AP may terminate for convenience at any time on 90 days' notice, and added a proviso confining any Kubient termination under that sentence to the end of the then-current Term. This is our fallback position; the mutual 90 days' notice and the fee entitlement are unchanged.

ops.oldText: Neither Party may terminate this Agreement during the Initial Term except as set forth in paragraph 4(b) or any Exhibit. Either Party may terminate this Agreement for any reason following the Initial Term upon ninety (90) days written notice to the other Party.
ops.newText: Kubient may not terminate this Agreement during the Initial Term except as set forth in paragraph 4(b) or any Exhibit. Either Party may terminate this Agreement for any reason upon ninety (90) days written notice to the other Party, provided that any termination by Kubient under this sentence shall be effective only at the end of the then-current Term.
